qc7ef1d56.question: Q-native-ceiling: Does the user require the inclusive estimated per-call budget with explicit native/tool/output/inspection reserves (a1, recommended and drafted), or a verified hard ceiling for every hidden native CLI request (a2, which blocks unverified autonomous CLI sessions)? The existing3-char/token estimator and official context/compaction settings do not prove a hard native ceiling. Do not implement until this approval preference is settled.
qc7ef1d56.choice: a1 — inclusive estimated per-call budget with explicit native/tool/output/inspection reserves
qc7ef1d56.rationale: The user explicitly approved the presented LLD and recommended inclusive estimated-budget policy with 'yes, approved'; a verified hard ceiling on hidden native CLI requests is not being claimed. Total execution time is10 minutes times current work chunks, retries do not reset time.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Enforce all-inclusive review budgets and exclude generated history

summary.prose: Make the configured128K allowance an inclusive estimated context budget for each review call, so instructions, schemas, native/tool overhead, completion and inspection growth reduce the material that fits. Reuse the existing evidence-preserving splitter and serial driver, exclude generated JSONL histories before review freshness selection, and record content-free per-call outcomes. Native CLI reservations are explicitly estimated, not measured or a proven hard ceiling; the stronger native-ceiling interpretation remains an approval question. Total execution time is10 minutes per current logical work chunk and is recalculated after subdivision, rather than frozen at the initial20-minute allocation.

api.signature: createReviewJob(adapter: ReviewAdapter<unknown>, path: ReviewPath, snapshot: ReviewMaterialSnapshot, limitChars: number, opts: CreateJobOpts & { budgetPolicy: ReviewBudgetPolicy }): ReviewPipelineJob

parameters.name: budgetPolicy
parameters.purpose: Required provider-qualified frozen policy, prepared before job construction at every production entry; never inferred only from configuration.

returns.meaning: Job whose every planned request fits the inclusive policy; same splitter/gather graph and deadline semantics.

errors.condition: Invalid policy, unqualified missing overhead profile, mandatory context or indivisible material cannot fit.

preconditions: Positive safe cap; execution profile/reserves available; adapter material stable.
The selected provider/profile or explicitly declared controller-reserved profile is available before any planning measurement.
postconditions: Cap is total context allowance, not payload allowance.
Every candidate includes enveloped messages and wire-schema allowance plus all reserves.
No required evidence is truncated or silently omitted.

parameters.name: job

Exactly one start and one terminal event per issued call.
No provider invocation after failed admission; no prompt/transcript logging.
ReviewBudgetError bypasses generic retry and stage partial-result policies; no exception may turn a refused budget into a successful review.

visualVerification.method: Local headless google-chrome rendered the generated file; screenshot inspected
visualVerification.result: Five participants and nine messages render; labels and order visible; rendered HTML itself remains unchanged.

contractDetails.controllerEmissionScope: All review-owned model requests and complete controller tool-response envelopes are admitted. Controller host conversation is outside daemon ownership and accounted only by explicit caller-declared estimated reserve; it is never a measured native total. The existing native-ceiling approval question determines whether that estimated mode is acceptable. Daemon source inspection still uses its qualified provider profile.
contractDetails.atomicStateNote: Controller continuations depend on NEW main-thread claim/commit operations across local and hub stores; existing read/update/release is explicitly not an atomic transition. Registered Zod schemas and final handlers are in scope.
contractDetails.timeBudgetRule: Total execution allocation =600000ms times current logical planned work chunks from one original start; retries do not add time and real subdivision/new stage work updates N. Per-attempt cap is min(selected existing execution limit, remaining job time), NOT a universally unchanged10 minutes. Code-review default is10 minutes; design-review defaults12/18/24 with a30-minute hard attempt ceiling. Dimensions remain independent jobs; report the sequential sum.

dataModelChanges.entity: ReviewBudgetPolicy (proposed, in-memory)
dataModelChanges.details: One frozen per-job policy owns totalTokens (existing review.chunkTokens, default128000), estimator='chars-per-token-v1' with3 UTF-16 text characters per estimated token, policyVersion, executionKind and explicit reserves. Proposed defaults: native/tool hidden framing16384 tokens, transport margin1024, completion including reasoning8192, plus24576 inspection/history tokens for reviewer sessions (0 for single structured calls). Packer retry headroom remains8000 characters, accounted once. These are engineering reservations, not observed native usage. Planning budget = estimated full enveloped prompt + wire schema + known tool definitions + native/transport/completion/inspection reservations + retry headroom; each inclusive sum <= totalTokens. At128K this leaves75157 estimated tokens before actual prompt/schema/known tools in a reviewer candidate. The exact budgeting choice is proposed for LLD approval; no claim that this estimator bounds actual tokenizer output. Production policy construction MUST receive a provider-qualified wire profile before planning; it cannot infer a provider from review configuration. No missing-provider production default is permitted. A profile is immutable serializable data, not a function in a frozen snapshot.

dataModelChanges.entity: ReviewBudgetBreakdown (proposed)
dataModelChanges.details: Immutable numeric fields: limitTokens, promptChars/promptTokens, schemaChars/schemaTokens, declaredToolsChars/declaredToolsTokens, nativeReserveTokens, transportReserveTokens, completionReserveTokens, inspectionReserveTokens, retryHeadroomTokens, estimatedTotalTokens, remainingTokens, estimatorVersion and qualification ('managed-estimate'|'reserved-native'). Do not use the word measured for native reserves. Measure complete provider wire schema or a proven conservative representation including strict-schema/envelope changes; unsupported normalization must refuse. Prompt, schema and tool text are counted once. Planning includes prospective retry headroom; dispatch counts an actual correction in prompt text and consumes, rather than duplicates, that headroom. Existing ReviewCall.chars stays serialized prompt length; add the breakdown separately. Every budget comparison, including gather/relation/duplicates, uses the shared total rather than local sentChars arithmetic.

dataModelChanges.entity: ReviewExecutionBudget on provider options (proposed)
dataModelChanges.details: Additive optional reviewBudget to ReviewSessionOpts and review-scoped structured completion options in src/shared/types.ts. Contains immutable policy, admitted breakdown, output allowance, native qualification and call identifiers, never source content. Managed Ollama loops remeasure all actual conversation/tool/schema text before every request and apply the supported output limit. CLI providers recheck final serialized prompt and schema, apply only documented and locally verified invocation controls, and identify their additional internal context as reserved-native. A missing/unsupported reserve profile errors explicitly; native context controls do not automatically upgrade qualification to hard-bounded. No config file rewrites or API credentials. Relationship ownership: one job owns one policy; one job issues0..N immutable calls; each call has exactly one admission breakdown and0..N managed-turn rechecks; providers consume copies, never mutate the job;0..N content-free progress events cite a call ID.

dataModelChanges.entity: ReviewCall lifecycle event (proposed)
dataModelChanges.details: Persist start/success/failure/cancel/refused event metadata through existing getLogger and existing progress callback. Fields: reviewId, dimension, stage, role, callId, chunkId/obligation key where present, attempt, provider/transport label, policy and estimator versions, qualification, budget breakdown, monotonic durationMs and stable outcome/errorCode. Omit prompts, schemas, source/transcript bodies, tool arguments/results, raw error messages and credentials; allowlisted error categories only. A terminal record is emitted in finally/error paths even when the whole dimension has no finished plan. Retain existing prepared/finished logs for compatibility. No new storage database or usage-artifact telemetry schema.

dataModelChanges.entity: Generated ledger changed-file exclusion
dataModelChanges.details: Extend existing flat .insrc/artifacts/*.json exclusion to flat generated *.jsonl alongside it. Apply before review subject/freshness and both graph/diff material assembly through the existing shared seam. Do not exclude nested .insrc/artifacts/templates/** or formats/**, user code/config, or user-authored nested JSONL. History remains stored and cited as provenance; exclusion only removes generated histories from code-change input and index freshness requirements.

dataModelChanges.entity: Provider wire-budget preparation contract (proposed)
dataModelChanges.details: Add an optional pure getReviewBudgetProfile capability to LLMProvider; existing CliProvider/OllamaProvider implementations return a validated serializable ReviewProviderBudgetProfile with providerId/transport/version, schemaDialect, declared tool manifest where observable, native/transport/output/inspection reserve values and explicit managed-estimate or reserved-native qualification. Missing capability is a typed native-budget-unqualified error for a budgeted production review, not an implicit zero-cost profile. Test providers supply explicit synthetic profiles. The profile selects the same pure schema normalizer used by the provider (Codex strict schema via existing codexStrictSchema in structured-output.ts; Claude JSON; Ollama JSON format). The single budget module measures the exact normalized wire-schema representation, not just the logical schema. Native hidden headers/tools remain a disclosed reserve, never hard-measured. Normalize on immutable copies and include the envelope wrapper. Production runDimensionJob in code-review.ts, grounded review in review/review.ts and runTemplateReview in review/template-review.ts all resolve the selected provider profile BEFORE createReviewJob, pass it in the frozen budget policy, and reuse/revalidate it at runReviewJob dispatch. The driver rejects mismatched provider/profile/normalizer versions. Controller step paths without an owned provider require an explicitly declared controller-reserved profile and must not claim to bound the host conversation; a missing profile refuses rather than bypassing admission. No provider SDK types enter shared application contracts.

dataModelChanges.entity: Required-neighbour evidence admission (changed existing fallback)
dataModelChanges.details: prepare.ts currently drops neighbour summaries using neighbours.slice(0,-1) if a singleton plus required usage evidence exceeds the hard limit. That branch MUST be removed for required call/reference evidence. Optional same-file/directory context may be added only while it fits, but required usage neighbours are never relabelled optional or omitted. If supported atom/relationship batching can preserve the complete required references it may be used; otherwise fail explicitly with required-context-over-budget before any model call. This is a deliberate correction to current behavior, not unchanged splitter reuse. Update the existing pipeline-job omission-expecting test to expect refusal, and separately prove optional context can be omitted without removing required relationship evidence. Preserve all core atoms and obligations; no smaller budget may silently reduce review accuracy.

dataModelChanges.entity: Correction admission and terminal budget errors (changed existing fallbacks)
dataModelChanges.details: ReviewBudgetError is a typed Error with stable code, stage/call IDs and numeric breakdown; it contains no prompt/schema/tool body. driver.ts MUST recognize it before generic classify/applyFailure and rethrow it unchanged after one terminal lifecycle event. It must never become transient, stall, record-not-judged or record-observation, even in grounded design-review verify stages. Replanning is allowed only as a deliberate earlier pure packing operation that preserves complete evidence; the driver does not catch a budget failure and quietly retry. In job.ts invalid-answer correction handling MUST replace the existing oversized-correction fallback: never reissue call.prompt without its required correction. Admit the full corrected prompt with consumed retry headroom; if it does not fit, explicitly replan with correction included and fresh call IDs where the stage supports complete evidence preservation, otherwise throw correction-budget-exceeded before a new issue/provider call. No fresh retry is issued from the old uncorrected prompt. Tests must cover both fail-review and record-not-judged/record-observation stage policies and assert no partial-success conversion.

dataModelChanges.entity: Review-scoped source-safe failure logging (changed existing logs)
dataModelChanges.details: Sanitize existing logs as well as new lifecycle events: driver.ts currently logs detail from err.message on failures, and CliProvider.runReviewSession logs err:msg on stall/transient paths before rethrow, even with internalRetry=false. For calls carrying reviewBudget, replace those source-bearing fields with allowlisted errorCode/classification, stage/call/chunk IDs, attempt, duration and numeric budget only. Audit review-scoped downstream subprocess/provider diagnostics for the same content-bearing fields; never forward raw reason arrays or provider/model error text to persistent review logs. Do not change unrelated non-review logging. The sentinel-leak test captures every relevant logger at driver and provider layers, including stalls, transient errors, invalid-answer corrections, refused admission and cancellation, rather than checking only the newly added event sink.

dataModelChanges.entity: Controller review emission budget and versioned continuation (proposed)
dataModelChanges.details: Cover BOTH controller implementations. Code review: src/daemon/steps/code-review-step/handler.ts emitJudgementsResult currently returns all dimension prompts plus grounding directly. Design review: src/daemon/steps/review-step/phases/start.ts directly emits buildTemplateReviewPrompt or buildExtractPrompt, while phases/claims.ts emits buildBatchedVerifyPrompt. These are review requests too and MUST NOT bypass inclusive admission. Add an optional reviewBudget declaration to both registered MCP input envelopes and corresponding input types: budgetProtocolVersion, declared hostContextReserveTokens and estimator qualification/profile ID. It is required only on controller-routed start/resume emissions; daemon-routed requests use the selected provider profile. The central policy factory constructs an explicit controller-reserved profile from that declaration, validates safe positive reserves and pins the server cap/version; a caller may lower its available budget but never raise the configured total. Missing, negative, malformed or unsupported declarations return controller-budget-required/unqualified before any prompt is emitted. Host reserve is caller-declared estimated context, not server-measured or proof of a native limit. No implicit zero-cost host or provider fallback. Every new controller input schema documents this qualification. In verified-hard-native mode an unverified external host is ineligible.

dataModelChanges.entity: Complete controller response accounting and subdivision (proposed)
dataModelChanges.details: Before emitting ANY controller-facing prompt/schema frame, estimate the entire final serialized tool response once, including all prompt blocks, schemas, grounding/metadata and state-token/framing text actually returned, plus declared host/native/output reserves. A response carrying four individually fitting dimension prompts is NOT admitted unless the combined frame fits. Never append an unmeasured whole grounding after admission. When an aggregate response is too large, drive the existing pure review-pipeline createReviewJob/nextCalls/applyOutput stages through versioned controller state and return one admitted pending call per MCP turn, using its actual callId/schema and only assigned material plus required context. Code-review dimensions aggregate only after every required chunk/gather/relation call completes. Controller replies use the new versioned callId/answer envelope in the existing judgements/findings/claims/verdicts outer phases; raw legacy whole-result replies cannot bypass the matching call/policy. Missing/duplicate/mismatched call IDs refuse. For template and extraction/verification design paths, reuse the corresponding existing adapters and evidence/claim-ID validators; perform deterministic evidence gathering only after the required extraction calls complete and retain every claim in verification/gather. An unsupported stage subdivision or indivisible mandatory frame must fail explicitly before emission; do not truncate, drop dimensions/claims or accept a partial completed artifact. Existing outer tool names/phases remain, but new controller continuation payloads are versioned and old controller clients need to supply the declaration/envelope contract.

dataModelChanges.entity: Controller budget resume validation (actual stores, proposed new state)
dataModelChanges.details: Persist budget protocol version, frozen server policy/profile, pending call IDs, required evidence snapshot and controller pipeline continuation only in the existing code-review-step and review-step state stores. This is a NEW continuation payload: current daemon pipeline jobs are ephemeral and current controller tokens contain subject/grounding or design intent/claims/evidence, not an already-persisted ReviewPipelineJob. Validate version/profile identity and current declaration before code-review start/confirm_wait/judgements resumes and design-review start/claims/verdicts/findings resumes. A fresh host-context declaration is required before each next emitted frame because the external conversation can grow; it can increase the host reserve or reduce room but cannot mutate the pinned server cap/estimator/native qualification. Pre-upgrade tokens without the new protocol fail review-budget-state-stale. Budget errors precede frame emission or final artifact write, do not trigger generic retry/partial-result policies, and do not consume a successfully reusable state on a mere missing declaration. Completed review artifacts are written only after all pending required obligations are validated; stale or replayed calls cannot complete the review. Existing read/update/release methods are NOT atomic replay protection. Use the new review-scoped main-thread claim/commit contract defined below; do not assume a worker-local mutex or read-then-release is sufficient. The server budgets what it emits plus the declared reserve; it does not know the host model conversation and must never call it measured or a verified128K native ceiling.

dataModelChanges.entity: Atomic review-state claim and commit (proposed additive store contract)
dataModelChanges.details: The existing SharedStepStateStore read/update/release operations are independent and provide no replay exclusion. Add review-scoped atomic operations on the MAIN-THREAD LocalStepStateStore and matching HubStepStateStore/stepStateHubHandlers bindings in src/daemon/threads/step-state.ts. Scope them to kind review or code-review; analyze/workflow lifecycle remains unchanged. Proposed typed operations: claimReviewState(kind, token, expectedGeneration, expectedCallId, internalRequestId) returns a structured-cloned payload plus an opaque server-minted claimId; commitReviewState(claimId, expectedGeneration, nextPayloadOrCompletion) validates owner/generation and atomically consumes the call, increments generation and updates/rotates the token according to its kind; releaseReviewClaim leaves state unchanged only when no external side effect has begun; invalidateReviewClaim makes the token terminal/uncertain after cancellation, owner loss or ambiguous persistence. Hub messages perform these transitions centrally, not as independent worker read/update calls. A worker-local lock or lease expiry alone is insufficient. Request/claim IDs are internal, not accepted as ownership assertions from the MCP caller.

dataModelChanges.entity: Atomic controller submission lifecycle and recovery
dataModelChanges.details: Validate missing/malformed budget declarations and outer input shape before claiming, so a missing declaration does not consume state. A non-consuming read for routing is allowed, but its generation/callId must be rechecked atomically by claim before accepting a reply. Only one request can hold a live claim for a pending call; concurrent duplicate submissions receive review-state-busy/stale with no model work or persistence. Revalidate profile, deadline, callId/answer and existing semantic checks on the claimed immutable snapshot; compute the next state before any write. Invalid reply/declaration detected before side effects releases the claim unchanged so the caller can correct it. For a non-final accepted call, commit pending-call consumption and next continuation atomically before emitting the next frame. For final completion, retain the exclusive claim across all awaited artifact validation/persistence and consume it only after persistence succeeds; no second request may persist concurrently. After success, keep a bounded TTL completion receipt (artifact/run/call IDs and status only) so replay returns already-completed without re-running persistence. If failure/cancel occurs before side effects with an explicit no-write guarantee, release unchanged. If a write may have happened, invalidate with review-state-uncertain and require inspection/fresh start; never automatically regrant or replay uncertain work. Owner worker/request loss signals cancellation and invalidates its claims; late owners are fenced by claimId/generation and cannot advance state. A live claim must not be evicted or made claimable by idle TTL/capacity sweep: pinned claims count toward existing bounds, and mint fails explicitly when all capacity is pinned. No automatic lease regrant while an old owner may still write. Completed receipts are bounded under existing store capacity/TTL and contain no source. Daemon restart still loses ephemeral tokens/claims; canonical artifact history is the recovery evidence, not a new database.

dataModelChanges.entity: Registered MCP schemas and terminal controller handlers (explicit change sites)
dataModelChanges.details: src/mcp/server.ts defines the actual Zod envelopes for insrc_review_step and insrc_code_review_step; add the reviewBudget declaration and the versioned callId/answer reply shapes there as well as the daemon input types. Keep outer phase names; document explicit refusal for legacy controller continuation payloads. src/daemon/steps/review-step/phases/findings.ts handleFindings and phases/verdicts.ts handleVerdicts MUST acquire the atomic claim, decode the new envelope, validate expected callId/generation/profile/deadline and only then hand answer to the existing template/verdict validators. Neither handler may validate/persist raw input.findings/input.verdicts as a bypass. Existing claim-ID completeness, source revision/lifecycle checks and other-party rules remain. Code-review handler judgements and both code-review full/degraded start/confirm_wait resumes use the same contract. review-step handler dispatch, start and claims paths propagate the declaration/state version. All final persistence is under the live claim and requires every pipeline obligation to have completed; no partial request can complete a review.

dataModelChanges.entity: Chunk-scaled review execution time (user-approved scope addition)
dataModelChanges.details: Replace the frozen-initial-session-count deadline in job.ts with explicit reviewStartedAt, timeBudgetUnitMs=600000, logical chunk/work-unit identity lineage, currentBudgetChunkCount, totalBudgetMs and deadlineAt. An unsplit model request is one work chunk. A work chunk is a distinct model request partition (source inspection, gather/reduce/obligation/relation or comparison stage) in the review plan, identified by stage/role plus logical chunk/key; a new callId for a retry/correction is NOT a new chunk. In a source-only initial plan,2 chunks mean20 minutes,5 mean50 and7 mean70. Every newly planned downstream model work chunk contributes once, and replacing a chunk on genuine subdivision removes its entitlement and adds its child leaf chunks; both completed leaves and still-pending leaves count. Superseded parents and failed retry attempts do not mint extra time; their elapsed time remains charged. Thus totalBudgetMs=600000*currentBudgetChunkCount, deadlineAt=originalReviewStartedAt+totalBudgetMs. It is NEVER now+newBudget and is not frozen at the first two chunks. Recompute before dispatch and after every source/stage/gather/reduce/relation subdivision and new stage plan; preserve lineage so unchanged/re-issued work cannot be counted twice. New units must correspond to a real admitted evidence partition or required obligation, not arbitrary IDs made to extend time. No-work deterministic-only jobs need no model execution budget. Safe-integer overflow/invalid lineage refuses explicitly. Individual provider attempts are capped at min(selected existing execution limit, remaining job time), with the existing30-minute hard attempt maximum, independently of the larger total. Retries do not restart either clock; cancel/deadline is checked before every call and finalization. Native size refusal may add genuine child chunks and update the total; unbounded repeated repartitioning is still constrained by existing evidence/attempt/size-reduction rules. This covers both reviewer-session and structured review calls and controller-issued work. Different dimensions remain independent jobs, each with this formula; report a sequential Story review total as the sum of its dimension job chunk budgets, never a misleading fixed20-minute whole-Story limit. Freshness/approval waits are separate from the execution budget and are labelled separately. Expired jobs are terminal: check the old live deadline before accepting an answer/failure, registering a subdivision or entering later work; a late response must not revive an expired review by increasing N. The initial zero-work preparation is the only pre-start case. New units planned while still active update the total from the same start epoch. At dispatch the driver arms an attempt timer for min(selected existing execution limit, remainingMs), combines it with cancellation, forwards the signal and races even a provider that ignores timeout options; structured and reviewer-session calls receive the same effective cap. No generation or tool wait may hold the driver past that cap. Controller emissions carry the deadline/remaining time, and late external replies are rejected; the daemon cannot kill an external host model process and must not claim that it did.

dataModelChanges.entity: Deadline reporting and transport qualification
dataModelChanges.details: Every prepared/replanned/start/terminal event reports currentBudgetChunkCount, timeBudgetUnitMs, totalBudgetMs, elapsedMs and remainingMs with the review/job IDs. The same frozen policy and original server-side execution epoch survive controller continuations; fresh host reserve declarations do not reset time. Timeout errors name the chunk count and derived budget (e.g. five chunks/50 minutes), not a hardcoded20 minutes. Existing per-attempt execution caps remain, clamped by the computed remaining total. Do not rewrite user config or silently substitute a fixed outer ceiling for the computed job budget. If an existing configurable stream ceiling is shorter than an announced computed allocation, report the incompatibility explicitly before more work is dispatched; do not claim the full allocation was available. External MCP transport timeouts (the observed300-second client wait) are distinct from daemon execution time; client disconnect may cancel according to existing cancellation policy, but it must not be reported as successful review or a20-minute job-cap failure. Persist paired outcome events so a lost client response can be diagnosed from the canonical run record. No new async workflow runner or hidden duplicate review is introduced.

dataModelChanges.entity: Trusted review-owner binding through actual request/worker lifecycle (proposed)
dataModelChanges.details: Extend the hub contract in src/daemon/threads/channel.ts to supply a trusted HubRequestContext alongside args for review state operations. It contains a per-connection nonce/worker generation from the main-thread WorkerConnection and a server-assigned active request-owner nonce. Existing generic handlers can ignore the optional context. The worker may identify the currently executing routed request, but cannot choose channel identity: serveHub binds that identity from its MessagePort closure, never msg.args. src/daemon/threads/main-services.ts ThreadServices.connectWorker must bind the per-connection handler context rather than use an ownership-blind shared handler set. src/daemon/threads/router.ts registers the internal request-owner nonce before dispatch and maintains its connection/worker-generation membership while active; claim operations validate both channel binding and active registry membership. A requestId or ownerId supplied in raw MCP inputs is never trusted. The owner nonce travels only in the internal execution envelope/context to the step host. HubStepStateStore forwards that internal nonce and the main thread verifies it against the bound connection before any claim/commit/release. Claims are bound to the trusted request plus connection epoch; another worker cannot commit/release a stolen claim ID or spoof request ownership. Local single-thread execution in src/daemon/steps/host.ts obtains a main-thread registered local owner from the same registry, tied to the server invocation and AbortSignal, and uses identical store checks; no worker-specific assumption is required. Review terminal handlers obtain this trusted execution context from server-controlled dependencies/step context, never from public input. Explicit carrier sites also include channel.ts RequestEnvelope/LocalRequestEnvelope and wireRequest, worker-requests.ts request dispatch/lifetime completion, worker-entry.ts execution-context wiring, daemon/request-context.ts trusted request metadata, and shared/step-context.ts out-of-band StepCallContext propagation into host.ts. Reuse the existing trustedContext/connectionExecution carrier conventions, not caller JSON. Only an opaque review owner nonce and worker generation crosses the worker wire; no session credentials or connectionSession/connectionExecution capabilities are serialized, and existing wireRequest refusal for those capabilities remains. The local host mints/registers its own trusted invocation owner where there is no routed worker; the worker host uses the router-registered nonce from the internal envelope and bound port context. Thread-service owner validation must reject a worker-supplied nonce that is not active on that exact connection. Raw MCP args cannot replace this carrier.

dataModelChanges.entity: Explicit owner-loss invalidation hooks (proposed)
dataModelChanges.details: In main-services.ts WorkerConnection.disconnect invalidates every owner/claim bound to that connection nonce BEFORE stopping hub service and closing ports; a new connection cannot reuse old ownership even if an OS/thread ID is reused. In supervisor.ts worker exit/detach and replacement call that invalidation hook for the detached worker generation. In router.ts explicit cancellation, failed dispatch, orphaned requests, terminal request completion and routed-request lifetime abort close the registered owner and invalidate its still-uncommitted claims according to the side-effect recovery rule. Current unary socket close intentionally does not cancel work; do not falsely report owner loss there while the request legitimately runs. Its internal owner remains until actual completion/cancel/worker loss. For single-thread steps, host.ts registers/unregisters the owner in try/finally and listens to its server AbortSignal. Normal finalization first commits state/completion receipt, then closes the owner; cleanup does not invalidate an already committed completion. If a request terminates with an uncommitted claim, make its token terminal/uncertain (or explicitly release only when the state machine proves no side effect started); never leave an abandoned pinned claim indefinitely busy and never grant a new owner while a former owner may still write. Reject late messages/commits after connection/request invalidation. Active unexpired owner claims stay pinned against ordinary TTL/capacity eviction, but lifecycle invalidation cleans them and bounded receipts prevent leaks. Tests must exercise these real hooks across local and two worker connections, not only direct store calls.

dataModelChanges.entity: Exact terminal verdict coverage (deliberate correction to current behavior)
dataModelChanges.details: handleVerdicts currently loops only over supplied verdicts, silently drops unknown claim IDs, accepts duplicates and can construct/persist a report from an empty or partial array. This MUST change: derive the immutable expected claim-ID set from the completed validated extraction state; for each versioned pending verification call derive its exact assigned subset. Before normalization/persistence require every expected ID exactly once, no unknown ID and no duplicate (including identical duplicates). The per-chunk answer must match its assigned subset, not merely any global claim; final continuation aggregation must equal the full expected set exactly once across all chunks/call IDs. Missing, empty-when-nonempty, duplicate, unknown, wrong-subset or malformed IDs produce verdict-coverage-invalid with zero persistence and no partial-success normalization. Do not log untrusted raw claim IDs/messages; use allowlisted categories and internal references. A genuinely empty expected set is permitted only after all required extraction chunks completed and the aggregate validated that no load-bearing claims exist; an empty reply cannot skip extraction or verification. Apply the analogous full expected-template-item check in findings aggregation before completion, preserving its existing strict validation. This is a new completeness guarantee, not a preserved one. Both registered MCP envelopes, final findings/verdicts handlers, code-review continuation aggregation and lifecycle persistence remain under the atomic owner claim.

dataModelChanges.entity: Separate attempt limits from new total-time allocation
dataModelChanges.details: The600000ms chunk unit is a TOTAL-budget multiplier, not a universal pre-existing attempt cap. Existing code-review session defaults are600000ms; design-review template settings currently default to12/18/24 minutes and HARD_REVIEW_DEADLINE_MS is30 minutes. Preserve the selected execution attempt cap from each role/configuration (and existing hard maximum), but give an attempt only min(that cap, chunk-scaled job remaining time). Thus one design chunk has a10-minute total and may be cut off before its old12/18/24-minute ceiling; that is an explicit new overall-budget behavior. Two design chunks have20 minutes total and one attempt can use its selected12/18-minute ceiling while the later attempt receives only what remains. Do not describe every design attempt as historically10 minutes. Update src/workflow/review/template.ts documentation/config-helper semantics: reviewDeadlineMs and existing designReview.timeLimitMs values provide the template attempt ceiling, not the new whole-job allocation. In template-review.ts separate the current limitMs/startedAt/timedOut reporting from the job budget; timedOut/deadlineError must report the live chunk count and derived total rather than closing over the old12/18/24-minute whole-review limit. design-review.ts template adapter and job.ts deadlineError must receive the current timing breakdown. Code and grounded review execution limits remain their existing role caps; all paths apply the new total formula. Keep stored config values and completed records unchanged; document the setting semantic change and update tests that previously assumed a whole-design-review complexity deadline or that source-session attempts always reach30 minutes. Do not silently clamp the whole chunk-scaled budget to the30-minute per-attempt safety maximum.

errorCases.scenario: Mandatory prompts, provider wire schema and reserves already exhaust the cap.
errorCases.detection: Shared estimator returns negative remaining material allowance before adapter packing or provider dispatch.
errorCases.response: Throw ReviewBudgetError with code mandatory-context-over-budget; emit refused metadata; make no provider call and retain all evidence for a fresh review.
errorCases.userImpact: Review explicitly cannot fit; no fabricated PASS or silent truncation.

errorCases.scenario: An indivisible atom or gather obligation cannot fit after overhead.
errorCases.detection: Existing packer requests singleton measurement through the inclusive estimator and receives total above cap.
errorCases.response: Preserve the existing explicit unsplittable failure with an inclusive breakdown. Existing relation/neighbour batching may split supported units; do not invent lossy truncation.
errorCases.userImpact: Names the structural unit category/ID and numeric shortfall without logging content.

errorCases.scenario: Correction, provider schema normalization or final closing instruction grows beyond the saved allowance.
errorCases.detection: Recompute final serialized request and effective wire-schema allowance at dispatch; compare with the frozen job policy.
errorCases.response: Do not send an oversized request. Use existing size-refusal/redivision only where evidence can be re-planned; otherwise fail once with dispatch-budget-exceeded. A retry has a fresh callId and same total cap.
errorCases.userImpact: No hidden oversized retry; terminal metadata identifies the attempt and budget.

errorCases.scenario: Managed inspection tool history or output grows beyond the next-turn budget.
errorCases.detection: Re-estimate accumulated conversation, advertised tools, closing schema/output reserve before each managed model request.
errorCases.response: Fail with inspection-budget-exceeded before sending the next request; retain evidence in memory until normal cancellation/cleanup, never truncate it or issue a partial-success review.
errorCases.userImpact: Review is unavailable until scope is split/restarted; diagnostics identify stage/turn without source text.

errorCases.scenario: Provider overhead profile is absent, malformed or claims unsupported hard-native guarantees.
errorCases.detection: Validate required positive/safe reserve values and qualification at budget construction and provider boundary.
errorCases.response: Fail with native-budget-unqualified. A reserved-native profile is always labelled an estimate; no context-window/compaction flag alone upgrades it to measured or hard-bounded.
errorCases.userImpact: Unqualified providers are not admitted under a false guarantee.

errorCases.scenario: Resuming an old controller review token with no declared budget version/profile
errorCases.detection: Actual code-review controller state in src/daemon/steps/code-review-step/types.ts and state-store.ts is subject/grounding and a step token, not a persisted ReviewPipelineJob. Add a budget protocol version/profile declaration to new controller state and validate it at the real resume boundary. Missing version in an old controller token is detected before prompts are emitted.
errorCases.response: Refuse the old controller token with review-budget-state-stale and require a fresh start. Daemon ReviewPipelineJob objects are ephemeral and are reconstructed for each new run; do not invent a persisted pipeline job migration or edit completed histories.
errorCases.userImpact: Only pre-upgrade in-flight controller tokens need restarting; fresh daemon jobs obtain the current explicit provider profile.

errorCases.scenario: Provider size refusal, stall, timeout, model error or cancellation.
errorCases.detection: Existing typed provider/pipeline error classification; cancellation signal and job deadline.
errorCases.response: Retain existing provider retry/redivision and per-attempt limits, while applying the user-approved10-minutes-per-current-chunk total deadline. Every attempt stays in the inclusive token policy and has one terminal event; budget errors remain fail-closed, and context overflow is never inferred from timeout alone.
errorCases.userImpact: Failures remain distinguishable from successful partial review. Existing per-attempt caps are preserved and clamped by remaining total; total time now scales with current logical work chunks as the user requested.

errorCases.scenario: Required neighbours or invalid-answer correction cannot fit
errorCases.detection: Full inclusive measurement includes every required usage neighbour and the actual correction text; existing omission fallbacks are not allowed.
errorCases.response: Remove the required-neighbour-dropping and uncorrected-reissue branches. Preserve all supported relationships through pure replanning, or throw required-context-over-budget/correction-budget-exceeded before another model call. Propagate the typed budget error without retry or partial-success conversion.
errorCases.userImpact: A review may refuse rather than silently lose correctness evidence.

errorCases.scenario: Controller response/frame exceeds the cap or a resume lacks valid budget declaration/version
errorCases.detection: At both controller handlers, validate the actual token store state and declared profile, then measure the complete final response before emit_claims/emit_findings/emit_verdicts/emit_judgements, not individual prompt fields alone.
errorCases.response: Return typed controller-budget-required/unqualified/state-stale errors without leaking prompts. Where adapters support complete subdivision, emit one budgeted pending call per turn with matching callId; otherwise refuse controller-frame-over-budget. No unmeasured grounding, omitted dimensions/claims or partial completed record.
errorCases.userImpact: Old controller clients/tokens require the new declaration/continuation contract or a fresh start; externally unverified native context stays explicitly qualified.

errorCases.scenario: Concurrent controller submissions or ambiguous final persistence
errorCases.detection: Atomic main-thread claim checks token generation, expected pending call and live owner before accepting a response; final handler retains claim through persistence.
errorCases.response: Only one owner proceeds. Missing declarations/invalid replies before writes preserve state; concurrent replay is busy/stale. After an ambiguous write/cancel/owner failure invalidate rather than regrant. Successful completion leaves a bounded receipt; replay never writes twice.
errorCases.userImpact: No duplicate final review from two workers; an uncertain completion requires inspection/fresh start instead of blind retry.

errorCases.scenario: Computed chunk-scaled budget expires or conflicts with an outer ceiling
errorCases.detection: Compare trusted server execution elapsed time with600000 times current admitted logical chunk count; check each attempt against remaining time. Validate safe arithmetic and announced outer limits.
errorCases.response: Recalculate on real plan changes without resetting the original start. Stop before another call/final write on expiry. Identify job expiry, per-call expiry, cancellation and MCP transport expiry separately. Surface a shorter outer ceiling as explicit incompatibility rather than silently clipping the promised budget.
errorCases.userImpact: Diagnostics show actual chunk count, total and remaining minutes instead of a fixed20-minute message.

migration.stateBefore: Analyzer passes UoQNS4qD-rHZ8Db5Q4Pzww and XLC5M2RvEbVmaSd3EsjEtA locate message-text sizing in shared job/envelope and independent gather/duplicate helpers. Configured128000 currently maps to384000 message characters. Review sessions have no inclusive budget option; managed tool history grows until turn/deadline limits. Flat generated JSONL enters the subject. Logs retain prepared/finished plans but not a terminal record for every call.
migration.stateAfter: One immutable inclusive estimated-budget policy governs initial planning, retries, gather/relation stages, dispatch and review-scoped managed turns. The full request and explicit reserves fit within the unchanged configured cap, and native qualification is visible rather than asserted as measured. Flat JSONL histories are retained as provenance but excluded from changed-code/freshness input. Every call has content-free start/terminal telemetry, including failed dimensions. The unresolved native-hard-ceiling preference must be settled before implementation is approved. Existing required-neighbour omission and correction-dropping fallbacks are corrected; typed budget errors bypass generic/partial policies. Profiles are prepared before planning. Existing review error logs are sanitized, not just new events. Atomic main-thread review claims prevent replay across workers; registered schemas and both final-answer handlers validate the new envelope before persistence. Total review execution time scales as10 minutes times current work chunks from one original epoch, including dynamic subdivision.

migrationSteps.action: Record the approved issue and new chunk-scaled time instruction, then settle the native-budget interpretation. Keep TU1 review on hold; do not modify global config or the128K cap. Existing per-attempt caps remain, clamped by remaining total; total job time is10 minutes times current planned logical work chunks.

Introduce explicit provider wire-budget profiles and additive review options. Resolve profiles before job construction at code-review, grounded-review and template-review entry points. Non-review defaults/completed records stay compatible; version actual controller step state and refuse pre-version controller resume tokens. Do not invent a persisted ReviewPipelineJob migration.

Switch all shared code/design review planning and execution paths to inclusive accounting, including provider schema preparation, managed tool turns and final answer. Add generated flat JSONL exclusion and paired content-free call events; run boundary, provider and real-git regressions. Integrate BOTH controller handlers at full/degraded code-review emission and design template/extract/verify emission, including complete-frame sizing, versioned continuation and actual state-store resume checks. Do not ship a daemon-only fix advertised as all-review coverage. Add the main-thread atomic review claim/commit and failure recovery contract, explicit MCP registration/final handler integration, and chunk-scaled time accounting with new fake-clock/concurrent tests before enabling the revised controller protocol. Propagate trusted connection/request ownership through main-services, router/supervisor and single-thread host lifecycle; add exact expected-claim/template-item coverage checks in terminal aggregation; separate template attempt limits from chunk-scaled job limits and their timeout messages.

Build and commit the reviewed fix, then push only its authorized changes so the daemon can update. Restart/update the installed daemon without rewriting user config and record its installed commit. In-flight old reviews must finish or be cancelled through existing lifecycle controls before restart; never edit live histories to fake completion.

Start one fresh TU1 review after the fix is installed. Verify inclusive budget breakdowns, excluded JSONL, call-level outcomes and policy qualification; retain any real failure and keep BUILD unapproved until the independent review succeeds or the user explicitly overrides.

migration.backwardCompat: No public IPC method or existing workflow artifact payload is replaced. Review budget options are additive and review-scoped; non-review provider/tool-loop callers retain existing behavior. review.chunkTokens remains the total configured allowance, now all-inclusive; no configuration file migration occurs. Existing ReviewCall.chars remains prompt-text diagnostics, with a separate inclusive breakdown. Completed old reviews remain readable; pre-version controller step tokens require a fresh start; daemon pipeline jobs are ephemeral, not persisted. Generated histories and all approvals remain intact. Controller MCP review inputs gain an optional declaration that is required when the server routes to externally executed prompts. New continuation replies are versioned callId/answer envelopes; old controller clients/tokens are refused explicitly and need updating/restarting. This behavior is not claimed to be transparent backward compatibility. Daemon-routed current callers do not need an external-host declaration. New atomic operations are review/code-review-scoped additions to the shared state store and its hub bindings; analyze/workflow token behavior remains unchanged. The earlier frozen-deadline/no-extension behavior changes only as explicitly authorized by the user. Old deadline tests must be revised, not waved through. The user's10×chunk TOTAL rule changes overall design-review deadline semantics: existing12/18/24-minute settings remain attempt ceilings, while aggregate job time follows the chunk plan. This is documented rather than labelled unchanged. Trusted owner binding is a scoped hub/host lifecycle addition; unary disconnect semantics remain as currently defined unless an actual cancel occurs.

alternativesConsidered.name: One inclusive estimated-budget contract over the existing pipeline
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Reuse the splitter and driver, subtract every declared overhead/reserve from the per-call cap, and expose estimation/qualification explicitly.
alternativesConsidered.approach: A single immutable budget policy and breakdown is consumed by all planning and execution paths. It counts the enveloped prompt and provider wire-schema allowance, plus explicit native/tool, completion and source-inspection reserves. Managed tool-loop turns remeasure their actual accumulated conversation before each call. Native CLI execution is labelled reserved-native, never measured or hard-bounded; unsupported/missing reserve profiles refuse rather than silently assume zero overhead. Generated histories are excluded by the existing flat ledger seam; content-free call events describe admissions and outcomes. No alternate planner or global configuration rewrite.
pros: Smallest cohesive change to existing graph-grounded infrastructure.
Preserves complete evidence through existing split/gather logic and reports all budget components.
Keeps CLI OAuth and current providers; no false native-token guarantee.
cons: Uses the existing token estimator; opaque native CLI internals remain an explicit reserved estimate.
Does not prove a hard ceiling for every hidden native CLI model turn; that stricter requirement needs a qualified provider protocol.

alternativesConsidered.name: Verified native-request ceilings with fail-closed provider admission
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Permit review only when every internal model request exposes a verified budget gate.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Use the same inclusive budget model but require provider execution to expose or prove bounds for native system/tool metadata, tool-result growth, output/reasoning and every request. Reject autonomous CLI sessions unless their versioned native context contract is actually verified. Managed local calls can be guarded directly. A flag called context window is not by itself sufficient evidence. This is the stronger interpretation of the unresolved native-ceiling preference.
pros: Can make a hard-bound claim only where it is supported.
Opaque or unqualified native contexts cannot silently exceed the claimed cap.
cons: Current CLI interfaces expose no verified per-request budget gate; source-inspecting cloud reviews may become unavailable.
More provider qualification work than the observed prompt-admission defect requires; must not invent CLI controls or silently downgrade critical review roles.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Choose this if the user requires a hard bound on every hidden native request. It may block current cloud review providers; no source/docs proof currently establishes that bound.

alternativesConsidered.name: Independent provider-specific planners and local thresholds
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Give each adapter and provider its own context accounting and subdivision rules.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Keep the current pipeline measurement and add separate prompt/schema/tool/output admission rules inside each provider and gather/retry helper. Each stage would independently shrink payload and define error behavior before execution. The current analyzer found multiple existing message-only sizing helpers; this shape would increase their independent policies rather than unify them.
pros: Localized changes can initially avoid reshaping the shared job contract.
cons: Multiple inconsistent budgets can admit planning calls that execution rejects.
More duplicated boundary logic across code/design review and provider variants.
Harder to show that the complete request is within the one user-configured cap.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Adds fragmented accounting to multiple existing helpers and cannot establish one all-inclusive admission boundary.

openQuestions: Q-native-ceiling: Does the user require the inclusive estimated per-call budget with explicit native/tool/output/inspection reserves (a1, recommended and drafted), or a verified hard ceiling for every hidden native CLI request (a2, which blocks unverified autonomous CLI sessions)? The existing3-char/token estimator and official context/compaction settings do not prove a hard native ceiling. Do not implement until this approval preference is settled.

sequenceDefinition.narrative: Shows where shared request accounting constrains planning and execution, and how managed inspection rechecks growth. It distinguishes reserved native CLI estimates from directly observed managed request text; no native hard-bound guarantee is implied.
